q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT P.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(EXPERIENCE_YEARS),2)AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT P JOIN EMPLOYEE E ON P.EMPLOYEE_ID = E.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY P.PROJECT_ID

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because Q1 uses an INNER JOIN, which means that only projects with at least one employee will be included in the results. On the other hand, Q2 uses a JOIN (which is equivalent to an INNER JOIN in this context), but the DISTINCT keyword is applied to the PROJECT_ID, which does not change the behavior in this case. The difference in results arises from the GROUP BY clause in Q1, which groups the results by PROJECT_ID, while Q2 also groups by PROJECT_ID. However, the DISTINCT keyword in Q2 does not affect the GROUP BY behavior, and the AVG function is applied to the EXPERIENCE_YEARS column in both queries. The difference in results is due to the INNER JOIN in Q1, which excludes projects without employees, while Q2 includes all projects, even those without employees.
